newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Explosion rocks Israeli military factory.
newsitem.headline: Explosion rocks Israeli military factory.

text.p: An explosion tore through a warehouse on Sunday at a factory near Tel Aviv where Israel makes parts for the U.S.-funded Arrow anti-missile missile, injuring at least one person, Israel Television said.
"I heard a huge bang and saw a giant black cloud billowing over the facility," a witness told Israel Radio.
Police said the blast occurred in a warehouse at an Israel Aircraft Industries (IAI) plant in the town of Beer Yaakov and one peron was treated for smoke inhalation.
A police spokeswoman gave no cause for the explosion but Israel and Army radios said the blast appeared to be an industrial accident.

Israel Television's military correspondent said state-owned IAI manufactures parts for the Arrow missile at the facility. The missile, designed to intercept incoming ballistic missiles was last test fired over the Mediterranean on March 11.

The Arrow is jointly financed by Israel and the United States. Security sources estimate the countries have poured $500 millon into the project since 1991. The projected cost is $1.6 billion but analysts say it could cost many times that figure.
Israel has been on high alert for suicide bombings by Moslem militants since an attack on March 21 in a Tel Aviv cafe killed three Israeli women.
